description: Castia-owned immutable local evidence, not a Foundry service wire format. No operation submits fine-tuning or implicitly deploys an agent.

hash.record_input: The normalized record object, including kind and schema_version, excluding the external artifact envelope id.

canonical_json.object_keys: string keys sorted by Unicode code point
canonical_json.numbers: Finite JSON integers and floats, preserving integer versus float representation; schema-v1 Python serialization uses json.dumps. This is not a claim of RFC 8785 compliance.

hash.source_file_input: Exact source bytes, never source file contents in the snapshot.
hash.candidate_file_input: Exact UTF-8 config content; CRLF and LF are distinct. Each file stores its validated sha256.
hash.example_input: The canonical JSON object containing exactly one key, input, with the reviewed/redacted input string.
hash.integrity_limit: Hashes detect content mismatch, not authorship. A writer able to rewrite the complete store can fabricate evidence; use access controls or external signatures across trust boundaries.

validation: Reject unknown record kinds, unsupported schema versions, unknown fields, duplicate JSON object keys, nonfinite numbers, and mismatched artifact identities.

Configuration and dependencies are explicit caller inputs, never environment dumps. JSON/YAML/TOML credential keys follow the same rules, including camelCase and quoted keys. Only whole environment/redaction placeholders or empty values are permitted at credential keys. Unsupported config formats fail. YAML parsing is lazy and requires the deploy extra. This is defense in depth, not a general secret detector.

Candidate embeds its evaluated AgentSnapshot, whose identity must match agent_id. Every staged payload path, exact content SHA-256 and byte size must match that snapshot's source_files. Capture staged config before evaluation; changed or unlisted files fail.
Paths are normalized relative files without traversal, absolute paths, drive roots, alternate data streams, symlinks, or Windows reserved aliases.
Artifact writes are immutable, idempotent, atomically published without replacing an existing file, and revalidated on read.
Collections are deeply immutable in memory; persisted records are normalized before identity calculation.

dataset.review: Every trace explicitly approved by a named reviewer before and after a versioned, caller-supplied redaction callback. Reference origin is an attestation, not an independently verified claim. deterministic means independently computed rule/test-fixture gold, not model output; synthetic control-flow evidence does not establish live model quality. Curated examples retain the sorted reference_origins of merged source traces.
dataset.model_output: Never persisted and cannot be reused as gold, including through the redaction callback.
dataset.deduplication: Exact reviewed/redacted input identity. Conflicting references fail; provenance and reviewers are merged.
dataset.split: Both train and heldout are nonempty, disjoint, and cover every unique example. Original and redacted conversation groups, including groups unioned by duplicate inputs, cannot cross splits.
dataset.determinism: Group ordering is by a SHA-256 rank of seed and group; input ordering does not alter the dataset identity.
dataset.rft_export: Local JSONL has a final user message plus independently reviewed reference and provenance. Export never submits a job.

evaluation.callback: Async callback(agent_snapshot, example, zero_based_repetition) returns a finite numeric metric mapping.

metrics.latency_seconds: Nonnegative; measured callback wall time is used if omitted.

evaluation.coverage: Every expected example/repetition pair is unique; comparison requires full successful coverage on both runs.
evaluation.cancellation: External cancellation propagates and joins all worker tasks. Callbacks must cooperate with asyncio cancellation. A timeout is failed evidence, not proof of remote cancellation: callbacks launching service jobs must cancel/poll only their owned jobs and persist terminal status or cancellation evidence; unresolved cleanup must be reported explicitly.
evaluation.exceptions: Persist safe error codes only, never callback exception messages or raw model output.

acceptance.decision: accepted is true exactly when reasons is empty.
acceptance.regressions: Sorted IDs of examples whose mean quality declined across repeated evaluations.
acceptance.fail_closed: Mismatch, missing/failed coverage, missing required metrics, nonfinite values or deltas, or any gate violation rejects acceptance. Explicit diagnostic gates may disable the default heldout requirement.

deployment.verification: Only literal boolean true returned by verify(candidate, deploy_receipt) advances known-good. A mapping receipt explicitly reporting failed, failure, error, cancelled, or canceled is rejected before verification. Receipts and exceptions are not persisted.
deployment.promotion: A candidate must match an accepted decision and extend the current known-good agent when one exists. Promotion is blocked while remote_state is unknown.
deployment.rollback: After failure/cancellation, first reconcile all possibly outstanding writes and then restore current known-good explicitly. After success restore the preceding verified candidate. Failed rollback does not move either known-good pointer.
deployment.concurrency: Mandatory expected_revision plus an exclusive lock reject stale or concurrent handoffs. Revisions advance once for start and once for completion.
deployment.recovery: Any handoff start, failure, or cancellation marks remote_state unknown and pending_cleanup true. No handoff, including rollback, may start while cleanup is pending. reconcile invokes an explicit verifier and records exactly {no_outstanding_writes:true,evidence:<nonempty terminal operation evidence>}; observing the active version alone is insufficient. Reconciliation clears pending_cleanup but does not change known_good or remote_state. Only a later verified handoff restores remote_state verified. azd timeout stops waiting and does not imply cancellation of Azure-side deployment. Stale locks and absence of a verified rollback target require external/manual recovery.
deployment.execution: Only injected deployment/verification callbacks execute. CLI adapters require local source and --allow-code; promotion/rollback additionally require --execute.
